notable_absence.finding: This page and its UI counterpart, geo-search-ui.md, do not link directly to each other anywhere in either page's text - unlike the simple-search pair in this same batch, where simple-search-rest-api.md links to simple-search-ui.md. Both geo-search pages instead link outward to the same set of supporting pages (customize-index.md, search-query-auto-complete.md), which is how the pair is actually joined in the corpus graph.

cross_component_finding: The REST and UI surfaces for building a geospatial-capable Search index document genuinely different underlying construction mechanisms for what is presented as the same outcome, not just a different client for one mechanism. This page has the user PUT a single JSON payload to the Search index REST endpoint with the field's `type` set directly to `"geopoint"` inside the mapping (`'geopoint' if your field contains GeoJSON data' comment aside`) - one API call, no intermediate index-building steps. Its UI counterpart, geo-search-ui.md, instead walks the user through [Create a Type Mapping](create-type-mapping.md) followed by [Create a Child Field](create-child-field.md), where the geopoint type is chosen from a **Type** list inside the Child Field UI action, after which the two pages converge again once a query is issued. Both apparently produce an equivalent index, but the documented paths to get there are structurally different (one JSON write vs. two chained UI actions each referencing their own separate reference pages) - worth flagging for reconciliation since it means 'search:create-search-index-rest-api' and 'search:create-type-mapping'/'search:create-child-field' are the REST and UI's respective real dependencies for this specific task, not a shared single mechanism underneath a REST/UI skin.
